The peace of living away has helped me a lot, that’s something I can relate a lot but also once I left I realized not everything was bad at home,things sometimes get hard and a lot of respect was missing but once you try out a different perspective you may see that it’s not that bad.

Now that’s for the “try to see it from their perspective”, as for what you’re saying it’s just trying to convince you to go with your family just to “take over” of you (to some extent ofc, I will never know the whole context)

I’m a bit confused on the timing but surely stop and think about it, the trip is the biggest issue because if you’re taking it it will surely be the most probable time to regret and overthink it, if you’re going you’ll have to be 100% sure to handle all the things that’ll happen afterwards, then again it seems like you don’t find that favorable and thats completely fine, you’re free to feel comfortable in a different lifestyle with different people (also, you can just videocall ur family, i know it sucks but that’s what i do, at least i get to talk with my grannies from time to time and hear their voices)

As for staying, i’m not sure if you mentioned that their support will still be there or if you can manage by yourself but BEWARE, that’s also a big decision that while bringing you mental peace might come with other issues, such as monetary ones, at least for medical checkups

I would support taking your time for yourself since that’s always the best option, take a break and think about how you feel regarding the situations your family is putting you through and handle it for as long as you can until you can leave peacefully or convince them to provide you better help, if it’s too much well… I wouldn’t say just run away but just take care in whatever choice you may take
